The interpreter is by far the most important part in Tums. It is the instance that parses your script.

## Creating Interpreters

1. Define an interpreter using `new Interpreter(Tusan language)`. With the language being the language you have created by using the previous steps, you can use `TumsAPI.getGlobalTusan()` if you want to execute the global language.
2. Set it up using `setup(InterpreterData data, TokenManager tknmanager, String _text, Path file, MinecraftEnvironment env)`.

That looks big doesn't it? Let's break it down:
- InterpreterData: Contains all the generated data (variables, functions, events, etc)
    - Define using `InterpreterData(HashMap<String, Variable> vars, HashMap<String, FunctionRegistry> funcs, HashMap<String, Variable> local, List<Runnable> asyncTasks)`
    - If you want to provide it anything in advance, for example a variable called `me` that gets the current player, you can instantiate a new Hashmap and add one.
    - You can provide them all as `null` and it will instantiate an empty interpreter data.
- TokenManager: You can provide a custom token manager if you want to execute a custom list of tokens
- String text: Optional, if you just want to execute a string of code, you can provide it here.
- String file: Optional, if you want to execute a file, you can provide it here.
- MinecraftEnvironment: This is the environment the script, by default `SERVER`
3. Optional: Set the context using `setContext(TusanContext ctx)`. This is applicable if you want to provide a custom [context](/tums/developer/context).

That's it! You're ready to start. Here's an example if you're still confused:

```java
public static void runScript(Path script, Tusan tusan, MinecraftEnvironment environment){
    Interpreter interpreter = new Interpreter(tusan);
    interpreter.setup(null,null,null, script, environment);
    interpreter.setContext(new TusanContext(interpreter)); // not necessary
}
```

## Executing Scripts

To execute a script just call `compile()` on the interpreter. __Or you could just use `TumsAPI.runScript(Path script, Tusan tusan, MinecraftEnvironment environment)` if you're not creating an interpreter__

```java
public static void runScript(Path script, Tusan tusan, MinecraftEnvironment environment){
    Interpreter interpreter = new Interpreter(tusan);
    interpreter.setup(null,null,null, script, environment);
    interpreter.setContext(new TusanContext(interpreter));

    try {
        interpreter.compile();
    } catch (Exception e){
        e.printStackTrace();
    }

    getRegister().add(interpreter.data);
}
```

## Methods

- `Interpreter(Tusan tusan)` - Creates an interpreter for a language
- `setup(InterpreterData data, TokenManager tknmanager, String _text, Path file, MinecraftEnvironment env)` - Prepares the interpreter to run a script. Any argument can be `null`
- `compile()` - Runs the script
- `setContext(TusanContext ctx)` - Uses a custom [context](/tums/developer/context) instead of the default one
- `error(String name, String detail, List<String> notes)` - Reports an error with the position it happened at, and stops the script by throwing a `ScriptError`, which `compile()` catches
- `arrowsAtPosition()` - Returns the code around the current position, with arrows pointing at the current token. Used by `error`
- `readFileContents(Path path)` - Reads a whole script file
- `meetEnd()` - Marks the script as finished, so nothing after the current token runs
- `clone()` - Returns a new interpreter set up with the same data and its own copy of the tokens
- `setLanguage(TusanLanguageRules lang)` - Replaces the lexer rules this interpreter reads the script with
- `getTusan()` - Returns the language this interpreter runs
- `getCompileEnvironment()` - Returns the environment the script runs in
- `setCompileEnvironment(MinecraftEnvironment env)` - Sets the environment the script runs in, `SERVER` when `null`

## Fields

- `Utils util` - Helpers for working with values and identifiers
- `InterpreterData data` - All the data the script has made: variables, functions, events, etc
- `TokenManager tokenManager` - The token manager, read about it in [Parsing](/tums/developer/node/parsing)
- `String text` - The script's code
- `String file` - The absolute path of the script file, or `<stdin>` when running code from a string
- `Object returned` - The value a `return` gave back, when running a function
- `Boolean isFunction` - Whether this interpreter is running a function's body
- `Boolean end` - Whether the script has finished
- `Boolean caughtError` - Whether an error has been reported
- `int pos` - The position of the current token
- `Token currentToken` - The current token
- `int loopDepth` - How many loops the current statement is inside. `break` is only allowed when this is above 0
- `boolean breaking` - Set by `break` until the innermost loop sees it and stops
